description: Supported `format` input on history tools (fill_history, order_history, position_history, cash_history, daily_balance_history). Controls the shape of the response body — default is 'objects' for backward compatibility.

formats.name: objects
formats.description: Default. One object per row with field names repeated on every row: `{items:[{symbol:"ESM6",qty:1,price:5800.25}, ...]}`. Readable and self-describing. Choose this for small result sets (< 20 rows) or when the agent only looks at one or two rows.

formats.name: columns
formats.description: Compact tabular form — field names appear once: `{columns:["symbol","qty","price"], rows:[["ESM6",1,5800.25], ...]}`. Rows are positional arrays aligned to `columns`. ~40–60% smaller on result sets > 50 rows. Choose this for large-range history queries (month+, every fill, every order).

notes: Same columns either way — only the shape differs. Every tool's output structure topic (e.g., describe(topic='fill_history_output')) lists the columns.
Unknown `format` values return a tool error with the valid-value list.
list_alerts does not accept `format` — its response is case-class-shaped, not ResultSet-shaped.
For monetary fields, null and 0 are different facts: null means the value hasn't been assessed yet, 0 means it was assessed and is exactly zero. Don't treat null as zero in a cost calculation.
